# SDK conformance cases

Cases every rpt SDK (Go in `sdk/`, Rust in `sdk-rust/`, Python in `sdk-python/`) runs in its tests, so the three read and write records the same way. An SDK for another language should run them too. All files are JSON.

- `stream.json`: reading a JSON Lines stream. Each case has an `input` string and, with `stop_at_error`, reads the way a writer or renderer does. `want` lists what the reader yields, in order: a record (`kind`, `raw` as received without its line end, 1-based `line`), a malformed line (`error_line`), or the error-level problem it stopped at (`stopped`, a record), after which nothing comes. The 16 MiB line limit is too big for a fixture; each SDK tests it on its own.
- `set_member.json`: setting one member of a record. `in` is the record's text, `member` and `value` what to set; `want` is the exact text that results, or `error: true` when it must be refused. A value is written compact, object members sorted by name.
- `round_trip.json`: decoding `in` as the typed record `type` and writing it again as the SDK's emit does. The result must equal `want` (or `in` when there is no `want`) as JSON, member order aside: unknown members survive, empty optional members are left out, required ones are always written, and a missing `kind` is filled in. Whether an empty list or object that was present is written again is left to each SDK, so no case has one. `type` is a record kind, or `description` for a `--describe` answer.
- `run.json`: the plugin entry point. `plugin` is a description and the candidates its completion function gives. Each case runs it with `args`: `describe` means stdout is the description as one JSON line (equal as JSON); `stdout` is the exact output; `runs` means the plugin's own function ran, with the same arguments. Everything not `runs` exits 0 without running the plugin. `no_usage` drops the usage from the description, `no_complete` the completion function; `complete_args` and `complete_word` are what the completion function must get.
